summary: This round-2 document re-review covers commit 1bdbd6b01bb5ce05a9047f663e1babf545baf2cc. All three round-1 findings are resolved, and no regressions or new blocking issues turned up. SEL-R1-01 (blocking) is resolved. I read evidence/repeat-spread.png directly: in the Storage × GPUs panel (job 45028778, sdfampere036, n=3), the Weka row reads 16.4% / 4.2% / 13.2% at 1/2/4 GPUs. That matches the corrected README line 39, the citation of page, panel, row and column, and the weka_one_gpu_repeat_spread entry in validation.json. SEL-R1-02 is resolved. README lines 45-48 now say the four-vs-eight-worker ordering reverses at batch 100, that four BDs × 16 workers/BD was not tested, and that four workers were chosen for lower provisioning at similar observed throughput. I checked these against heatmaps.txt lines 20 and 69 (about 1,551 vs 1,580 events/s, -1.8%) and against REPORT.md lines 85 and 172-177. SEL-R1-03 is resolved as documentation. validation.json records the seed, Python 3.11.14, the method, all 18 (case, block, count) tuples, the CSV SHA-256 and matches_saved_csv=true. I compared the recorded tuples with sweep.csv row by row and they match. I did not run the regeneration or recompute the hash myself. The selected profile is unchanged (4 BDs on 1 GPU, 4 workers/BD, batch 200, 1 stream, 1 MiB tasks, 16 MiB bounce, 512 KiB bulk), the CSV is still a stripe-only 3×6 complete-block design, and the scope and limitation statements are kept. status.json and README lines 10-15 still describe the pre-re-review state ('awaiting re-review'). That was accurate at this commit, but the coordinator should update them when recording this verdict.
checks: SEL-R1-01: I read evidence/repeat-spread.png myself. The Storage × GPUs · 4 total BDs panel (45028778 · sdfampere036 · n=3) shows Weka at 16.4% / 4.2% / 13.2% and NVMe at 1.7% / 4.0% / 1.6% for 1/2/4 active GPUs. The README value of 16.4% and its citation (page 3, Storage × GPUs panel, Weka row, one-GPU column) are correct. The figure title matches REPORT.md's repeat-spread section: 7 cohorts, 48 configurations, 102 full runs.

SEL-R1-01: validation.json weka_one_gpu_repeat_spread records 16.4, the source location, a manual visual check that was not recomputed from raw CSVs, the render path and a render SHA-256. I did not recompute the render hash.

SEL-R1-02: README lines 45-48 add the reversal at batch 100, the untested 4 BD × 16 workers point, and the lower-provisioning rationale. In heatmaps.txt line 20, the reversed-text cells for 4 BDs at batch 100 decode to 1,551 vs 1,580 events/s. Line 69 decodes to -1.8% vs the 0.0% control. REPORT.md line 85 says 4 BDs × 16 workers needs 82 cores and was not run.

SEL-R1-03: The case_block_count_order in validation.json matches sweep.csv row by row. Block 1 is 2,16,32,8,1,4. Block 2 is 16,1,32,8,2,4. Block 3 is 2,4,8,16,1,32. Each block holds exactly {1,2,4,8,16,32}.

Regression check on sweep.csv: 18 rows, and every non-stripe column is constant: stripe size 1048576, 100000 events, 4 BDs, 1 GPU, 1 stream, 4 workers, batch 200, 524288 bulk, 1048576 task, 16777216 bounce, 6 GiB, 34 cores.

Regression check on README: the fixed configuration table matches the original selection and REPORT.md's recommendation. Every comparison stays within one cohort. The worker cohort (5.1150 GiB/s) and the later Weka cohort (4.7839 GiB/s) are kept separate. Upstream review status is stated correctly: 4 cohorts passed, 3 pending, and the synthesis has no verdict.

Regression check on README: the stated limitations remain. The raw cohorts were not audited, the Perlmutter 34-core map is still a proposal that needs allowed-mask qualification, harness/auditor adaptation for batch 200 and 4 workers is still required, peak memory telemetry and the bounded launcher are still prerequisites, the sizing run is excluded from ranking, and there are no Lustre-optimum, cube or multinode claims.
Arithmetic carried over from round 1 is unchanged: 6+4×(4+3)=34, 16×16 MiB=256 MiB, 335,820,000,000 B = 312.756747 GiB, and 21600-3042=18558 s = 5h09m18s.
status.json and review-block.json record the user's explicit approval for the external review. bypass_attempted is false.
limitations: I ran no commands. I did not run the random.Random(20261115) regeneration, the sweep.csv SHA-256, the render SHA-256, the source hashes in provenance.json, or git diff --check. These rely on the coordinator's recorded results. I independently checked only that the recorded tuples match the CSV rows.
I did not render the original heatmaps.pdf. The 16.4% check relies on the supplied repeat-spread.png, and I did not verify by hash that this PNG was rendered from the unchanged source PDF.

Raw CSVs, comparisons.json, figure tests and upstream cohort reviews were not supplied. I did not audit the native cohort results again. The task-size, bounce-size and storage/GPU cohort result reviews are still pending, and this review does not close them.

I did not inspect Perlmutter CPU/NUMA inventory or Slurm allowed masks. The 34-core disjoint mapping, the harness and auditor adaptation for batch 200 and 4 workers, and memory-headroom qualification all still need to be done before execution.
This revision is document-only, so no runtime or code tests apply, and none were run.
I did not re-read PLAN.md, implementation/README.md or implementation/status.json in this round. Supersession was verified in round 1, and the stated scope rules out changes to them.
